name: American blackface-style clean (6L6 pair)
notes: Mid-60s American clean style: sparkling highs, deep scooped mids, lots of headroom. Path: V1a -> tone stack driven straight from the plate (no cathode follower) -> volume -> V2a -> phase inverter (12AT7) -> 2x 6L6GC with strong feedback and no presence control. FROM SCHEMATICS (fairly sure): 12AX7 stages with 100k plate resistors and 1.5k/25 uF cathodes; tone stack 250p treble cap, 0.1u bass cap, 0.047u mid cap, 250k treble and bass pots, 100k slope resistor, a fixed 6.8k resistor instead of a mid pot (so 'mid' is set to 10), driven from the plate (about 38k source); 12AT7 long-tailed pair phase inverter; 6L6GC pair. UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: the real amp has a reverb mixing stage between V2 and the phase inverter; it is left out and only its loss is kept (-18 dB, a guess: without it the phase inverter was overdriven and the preset distorted 26% when played hard); phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage); feedback amount (set for about 10 dB); output into 4.2k. POWER SUPPLY: GZ34 tube rectifier plus the winding, as 170 ohm into 70 uF (supply_ohms, supply_uf on the power block), so the sag comes from the current the power tubes really draw. These two values are GUESSES from typical parts, not from this amp's schematic. (It replaced a sag block.)
